This document provides a general overview of the final design presented during a Final Design Review during the conclusion of the project’s first budget period. This report includes a general description of the MTV design and explains the main system requirements that have driven it. Later, an overview of the design process conducted for the hull and structural designs is presented, and the stability of the achieved design is evaluated. The general arrangement of the MTV is also explained, serving as an introduction for the description of a current energy converter (CEC) supporting structure design. Mooring options designed are then presented, as well as the ancillary, control, and electrical systems’ design. Next, marine operations are briefly defined, followed by a section dedicated to a Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) and a risk register update. Finally, FAU developed plans for MTV permitting and operation, which are summarized in this report. The Permitting Plan developed a strategy to leverage regulatory approvals needed to commission the MTV to help reduce regulatory concerns related to the MTV platform itself. The Business Plan presented a method to understand the MTV’s operational modes and potential personnel interactions. It then explored costs associated with cost of operation and cost of ownership and a strategy to manage and maintain an MTV in service for the marine energy sector in the U.S. As-built construction quotes were collected from several U.S. and international shipyards for the MTV final design selected by DOE. However, due to the significant global changes to the supply chain and material availability post-2019, quoted costs were 3-5x greater than the budget allocated for construction ($3.9M). Therefore, it was mutually agreed by the project team and DOE to terminate the existing project and identify the additional funds needed for a future project to build and commission the MTV. Final Technical Report 9/57 1 INTRODUCTION This document summarizes the MTV's complete design, describing each subsystem's main features and design processes followed. This report aims to present the reader with a self-contained overview of the capabilities and characteristics of the vessel so a complete understanding of the MTV can be obtained. It describes the main dimensions of the vessel and the conditions under which it can operate and be moored, making a particular analysis of the selected sites. Also, the justification of the diverse subsystems’ design is presented together with the strategy for their operation and the risk register and FMEA. During the preliminary design review (PDR), three design alternatives were presented, each representing a design on a spectrum of basic to full capabilities, and their associated costs were estimated.
